audit_findings.title: Gross cash may include customer-funded operating cash
audit_findings.magnitude: up to $4.333 billion, or $15.42 per share and 6.9% of the $63.125 billion base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: The bridge adds cash directly to equity value; customer-funded or minimum operating cash is not excess cash and its later working-capital unwind may also reduce OE.
audit_findings.evidence: In some instances, we receive advance payments or deposits from our customers, which help fund our purchase commitments and reduce collection risk.
audit_findings.explanation: The bridge demonstrably adds the entire $4.333 billion cash balance, while the same filing reports $11.034 billion of current customer advances and deposits plus $2.607 billion of noncurrent commercial customer deposits. This does not prove that all cash is unavailable, but it leaves a potentially material bridge overstatement because no amount has been demonstrated to be excess.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile July 2026 cash to contract liabilities, restricted balances and minimum operating liquidity, then rerun all scenarios using only documented excess cash and any required working-capital unwind.

audit_findings.title: Estimated variable consideration may overstate owner earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: unquantified (the filed $1.3 billion net unbilled receivable is the exposure base, not an earnings-loss estimate)
audit_findings.mechanism: Unrealized variable consideration can inflate reported profit in historical OE years and therefore the normalized OE anchor and every projected cash flow.
audit_findings.evidence: It is reasonably possible that the actual amount of variable consideration realized could be less than our estimate, which could have a material unfavorable impact on our results of operations.
audit_findings.explanation: This is an unresolved estimation risk, not a demonstrated misstatement. The July 2026 filing repeats that realization below management's estimate could materially harm results, and the related net unbilled balance remained $1.3 billion. Because the embedded profit, affected OE years and collection probability are undisclosed, the valuation effect cannot be quantified, but the issuer's material-impact warning makes it reasonably capable of changing the valuation.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the contract-level variable consideration, recognized profit by OE year, customer acceptance evidence and subsequent collections; probability-weight unsupported amounts and rerun the OE trend, anchor and scenarios.

audit_findings.title: Underfunded pensions may be an omitted senior claim
audit_findings.magnitude: $763 million year-end deficit; $537 million 2025 contribution, including a $293 million prepaid 2026 contribution
audit_findings.mechanism: Any unrecovered pension funding belongs either as a recurring cash reduction to OE or as a senior-claim deduction in the equity bridge, without double counting.
audit_findings.evidence: We contributed $ 537 to our qualified pension plans in 2025, which is reported in other operating activities in our Consolidated Statement of Cash Flows.
audit_findings.explanation: The $763 million deficit alone equals about $2.72 per share and 1.2% of base equity value, but the cash-flow issue could be larger: the $537 million contribution was 13.6% of the $3.9595 billion OE anchor. Materiality remains unresolved because $293 million was an early contribution and substantial government-plan costs may be contractually recoverable; the record does not identify the normalized unrecovered burden or whether OE already captures it.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile each OE year to actual pension cash contributions, remove timing prepayments, separate government-recoverable amounts from commercial and non-qualified obligations, and rerun OE or the bridge for the unrecovered amount only.

audit_findings.title: Potentially material antitrust liability is unquantified
audit_findings.magnitude: computed $0 current claim exposure after dismissal with prejudice, versus $63.125 billion of base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: A surviving litigation obligation would reduce the equity bridge, but the identified claim no longer survives against General Dynamics or its subsidiaries.
audit_findings.evidence: Depending on the outcome of this matter, there could be a material impact on our results of operations, financial condition and cash flows.
audit_findings.explanation: The earlier 10-K described an unresolved potentially material claim, but the latest supplied 10-Q reports that plaintiffs dismissed the case against General Dynamics and its subsidiaries with prejudice on May 18, 2026. On the supplied record, this specific contingent claim therefore contributes zero prospective valuation exposure and requires no valuation deduction.
audit_findings.action: Retain the dismissal order and confirm that dismissal did not involve an unrecorded settlement, indemnity or continuing payment obligation; absent such evidence, no rerun is needed.

audit_findings.title: Off-balance-sheet performance arrangements could become cash claims
audit_findings.magnitude: $2.1 billion at July 5, 2026, or $7.48 per share and 3.3% of base equity value if fully called
audit_findings.mechanism: A probable call, collateral restriction or cash payment would reduce available bridge cash or future OE.
audit_findings.evidence: In the ordinary course of business, we have entered into letters of credit, bank guarantees, surety bonds and other similar arrangements with financial institutions and insurance carriers totaling approximately $ 2.4 billion on December 31, 2025.
audit_findings.explanation: The arrangements are existing contingencies, but their $2.1 billion gross face amount is not a recorded loss and does not establish expected cash exposure. The amount declined from $2.4 billion at year-end, and the filing provides no call history, collateral or probability information. A full call would be measurable but unlikely to represent the economic exposure, so present materiality remains unresolved.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the July 2026 instrument schedule, beneficiaries, collateral and restricted cash, expirations, historical calls and probability assessments; deduct or scenario-weight only probable unreimbursed exposure and rerun the bridge if identified.
